\section{Gaussian Space --- Surface Area}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.SurfaceArea
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Surface Area: Introduction}
The rotation definition gives an extended Gaussian perimeter, with a genuine right limit, null-set invariance, halfspace values, and isoperimetric bounds.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Surface Area: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Secant slopes and right-hand liminf]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.subadditive_quotient_le_liminf}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(0)=0$, be continuous at $0$, and obey
$f(s+t)\le f(s)+f(t)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$. For every $\delta>0$, the extended
nonnegative real number obtained by truncating $f(\delta)/\delta$ below at zero is at
most $\liminf_{t\to0^+}$ of the similarly truncated quotients $f(t)/t$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\delta>0$. Then
$\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(\delta)/\delta\le P_\gamma(A)$, where $s_A(\delta)$ is the rotation
sensitivity of $A$ and $P_\gamma(A)$ is its Gaussian surface area defined by the lower
limit of the positive-angle quotients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of the rotation perimeter limit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.surfaceArea_rotation_limit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_quotient_le_surfaceArea}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p019-b001}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. For every measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t]_+\to P_\gamma(A)$ as $t\to0^+$, with convergence in $[0,\infty]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Sensitivity invariant under Gaussian null changes]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_congr_ae}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ agree almost everywhere
with respect to standard Gaussian measure: for almost every $z$, $z\in A$ if and only if
$z\in B$. Then for every real $\theta$, their Gaussian rotation sensitivities are equal:
$s_A(\theta)=s_B(\theta)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariance under Gaussian null changes]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.surfaceArea_congr_ae}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_congr_ae, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge 0$, and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. If $A$ and $B$ agree
almost everywhere with respect to standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, then their
Gaussian surface areas are equal.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$, and let $t\in\mathbb
R$. The Gaussian surface area of the halfspace $\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i
z_i\le t\}$ is $\varphi(t)$, the standard Gaussian density at $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rotation quotient bounded by Gaussian surface area]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_le_surfaceArea}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_quotient_le_surfaceArea}
\proofsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p020-b001}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\delta>0$. Then
$\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(\delta)/\delta\le P_\gamma(A)$, where $s_A(\delta)$ is the rotation
sensitivity of $A$ and $P_\gamma(A)$ is its Gaussian surface area defined by the lower
limit of the positive-angle quotients.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perimeter lower bound from Gaussian volume]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.surfaceArea_volume_lower_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_le_surfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_pi_div_two, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p020-b002}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable with $\alpha=\gamma_n(A)$, then $2\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\alpha(1-\alpha)\le P_\gamma(A)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gradient integral bounded by Gaussian surface area]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gradient_le_surfaceArea_of_variation_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le_of_integral_variation_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_le_surfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $f:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $D(x)$ at every $x$, with $D$ continuous and $0\le
f(x)\le1$ for all $x$. Suppose that for every real $\theta$, the Gaussian product
integral of $|f(X)-f(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)|$ is at most the rotation sensitivity of
$A$ at $\theta$, where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors. Then the
Gaussian integral of $\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(x)e_i)^2}$ is at most the Gaussian surface
area of $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian isoperimetric bound from averaged profiles]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.isoperimetric_of_averaged_profile_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_profile_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let
$0<\alpha<1$. If, for every $u\in(0,\pi/2)$, the extended nonnegative value of the
closed Gaussian profile at $\alpha$ is at most the extended nonnegative value of its
integral over the averaged Gaussian indicator of $A$ at angle $u$, plus the Gaussian
surface area of $A$, then the extended nonnegative value of the Gaussian isoperimetric
profile at $\alpha$ is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Isoperimetry from regular averaged indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_isoperimetric_of_averagedRegularity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_rotation_variation_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_bobkov_smooth_le_sum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianGradient_of_bounded, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.isoperimetric_of_averaged_profile_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gradient_le_surfaceArea_of_variation_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and suppose
its standard Gaussian measure has real value $\alpha\in(0,1)$. For every
$u\in(0,\pi/2)$, define $f_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos(u)x+\sin(u)y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. Suppose that
for each such $u$ there are a continuous-linear-functional-valued map $D_u$, a constant
$C_u\ge0$, and a real number $M_u$ such that $D_u(x)$ is the derivative of $f_u$ at
every $x$, $D_u$ is globally Lipschitz with constant $C_u$, and $\|D_u(x)\|\le M_u$ for
every $x$. Then the Gaussian profile $U(\alpha)$, converted to an extended nonnegative
real, is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$, defined by the lower limit of its
scaled rotation sensitivities as the angle tends to zero from above.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian isoperimetric inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_isoperimetric}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianSurfaceArea, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_isoperimetric_of_averagedRegularity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_fderiv_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_fderiv_averagedGaussianIndicator_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let
$\alpha\in(0,1)$ equal the standard Gaussian measure of $A$. Then the Gaussian profile
$U(\alpha)$, converted to an extended nonnegative real, is at most the Gaussian surface
area of $A$, defined by the lower limit of its scaled rotation sensitivities as the
rotation angle tends to zero from above.
\end{theorem}
